The remarkable tale of how Keogh saved Hitler’s life will be revealed in a forthcoming Radio 1 documentary series—inspired by the book.
While Hitler stayed in Keogh's Munich barracks, he also visited Keogh's home and even received a glass of poteen in Kildare village.
At the close of World War I, Keogh's father deserted the British army, maintained his family in Ireland, and defected to the Irish Army, which was battling on the side of Germany’s ally, the Ottoman Empire.
The life story of Michael Keogh is certain to fascinate. We are likely to learn more about his ordeal on Radio 1 soon.
